Generated by `python -m experiments.make_phase2_lodo_report` from the LODO tables (`combined/`), which are rebuilt from cell artifacts only. Numbers are facts; interpretation and the final rebuttal wording are written by hand.

## Coverage and gates

* cells written: 48 of 48 (main protocol 42 of 42; Electricity sibling sensitivity 6 of 6); target datasets with a main cell: 14 of 14

* every tabulated cell passed all of its reproduction gates (full model vs Phase 1 and H3, hard cut and dataset-specific adapter vs H3, test rows, identity adapter); the table builder refuses a cell that did not
* pre-fit preflight (latest job 9229954): 42 of 42 (target, depth) pairs passed

## Main protocol: test MASE change vs the full model (median [IQR] over datasets)

Speedup = the measured end-to-end Chronos-2 adapter speedup at batch size 1 from the committed Phase-2 latency runs (same adapter shape, so it carries over). `pooled < hard` = datasets where pooled transfer beats the hard cut (point estimate / paired 95% CI excludes no improvement). Gap closure = median share of the hard-cut MASE gap recovered, over datasets whose hard-cut gap CI is above 0.

## Fixed limitations (stated independently of the outcome)

* The truncation depth (L4, L6, L9) is fixed in advance. Choosing a depth on an unseen dataset without calibration data is a different question, not answered here.
* Unseen DATASET is true for every main cell; unseen SERIES is true for every main cell (the Electricity sibling is excluded) and false for the sensitivity cells. For targets listed as Chronos-2 pretraining data the frozen backbone may already know the series; 'not listed' means undocumented, not unseen. Only the held-out group is unseen by the backbone as documented.
* One adapter fit per cell (seed 0); variation across seeds is not measured. Sources weigh equally in the objective and in the selection criterion, whatever their size.
* Chronos-2 only; the label-free objective matches the full model's own head outputs, so a pooled adapter cannot exceed what the full model forecasts.
